title: Cyber harassment at the workplace - overlap with sexual harassment law
p1:
A harmful message sent after office hours can still become a workplace issue.

Many people think harassment only happens inside the office or through face-to-face actions. But digital spaces have changed the way workplace misconduct can occur.
p2:
A surprising fact: online behaviour can sometimes fall under sexual harassment rules even when it happens through chats, emails, social media, or messaging apps.

The key question is not just where it happened, but whether the conduct is connected to the workplace and creates an unsafe, hostile, or intimidating environment.
p3:
Cyber harassment may include unwanted sexual messages, sharing inappropriate content, repeated online advances, or misuse of digital platforms against a colleague. Employers are expected to take complaints seriously and follow applicable workplace harassment procedures.

The practical takeaway: workplace boundaries do not disappear when communication moves from a meeting room to a screen.
conclusion: Do you think companies are doing enough to address harassment that happens through digital channels?
